title: Double-Breaded Chicken Cutlets
summary: Brined, evenly pounded cutlets with a two-layer crust that stays crunchy even when reheated.
difficulty_reason: Overnight brine, two-stage breading and deep frying in batches at a steady temperature.

ingredients.line: 2 large chicken breasts, sliced into cutlets
1 cup all-purpose flour, seasoned with salt and pepper
About 2 inches of vegetable oil, for frying

steps: Stir the water, salt, sugar and MSG together until dissolved, add the chicken and refrigerate overnight.
Remove the chicken from the brine and pat it dry. Slice the breasts into cutlets.
Pound the cutlets just until they are an even thickness throughout, not paper thin.
Dredge each cutlet in seasoned flour, dip it in egg, then coat it in the Italian breadcrumbs.
Dip the cutlet back in the egg, then coat it in panko.
Heat 1 to 2 inches of oil in a Dutch oven to 350°F.
Fry the cutlets one at a time for 3 to 4 minutes each, keeping the oil at 350°F, until golden and cooked through.
Drain on a rack and serve hot.
tips: Aim for even thickness, not thinness, so the chicken cooks at the same pace as the crust.
Use plenty of oil so the temperature holds when the cutlets go in and the breading doesn't turn greasy.
missing: Amounts for the flour, egg, breadcrumbs, seasoning and oil weren't given and are estimated.
